description:
Writes the site plan (.xodia/plan.json) on a branch, saved at once like every edit. Send one of: plan with the whole plan or only the top-level fields you change (brief, inspiration, brand, audience, goals, motion, sitemap, pages, globals, library; the rest keeps its values; pages merge by path, so send only the pages you change; renaming or removing a planned page updates the nav and footer), pageStatus to set pages to planned, wireframed or built (one { path, status }, or a list), or globalsStatus for the shared nav and footer. Statuses are read from the site, so pageStatus and globalsStatus are optional: Xodia sets them when a request finishes and on sync_site_plan. With plan, always pass the etag from your last get_site_plan (null when there was no plan): if someone changed the plan since, it answers plan_conflict and you read again. pageStatus or globalsStatus alone needs no etag (they set one field on the plan as it is now); an etag you do pass is checked. Refuses a plan that isn't valid with each problem and where it is, and refuses renaming or removing a page that is on the site with 409 page_on_site (nothing written): move it with move_page, which carries its plan entry, or remove it from the site first with delete_page and then call sync_site_plan. Keep the user's brief and inspiration notes as they wrote them. Limits: 40 pages, 4 levels, 20 sections a page, 5 inspiration sites. Every field is optional and defaults to empty. Fields (lists in brackets are the allowed values):
brief {name, business, audience, markets[], locales[], look, existingContent, links[] {url, label}}: the user's words, keep them.
inspiration[] {url, likes[] (layout, colours, fonts, tone, motion), note, takeaways, reachable (true, false or null)}: the user writes url, likes and note; you write takeaways and reachable.
brand {name (from brief.name, never invented), pitch, toneOfVoice, colours[] {name, value (#hex), role (suggested: primary, secondary, accent, background, surface, text, muted, border)}, fonts[] {family, role (heading, body, accent, mono), source, locale?}, logo (a repo path or null), iconSet? (the site's one icon set: lucide, tabler, heroicons, phosphor, iconoir, mingcute, material-symbols, radix, bootstrap; left out: keep the site's own set, else lucide)}. Fonts are one per role and locale: a font with a locale (one of audience.locales) serves that language beside the default one.
audience {markets[], personas[] {name, description, needs}, goals[], locales[] (language codes, default first)}.
goals {primaryAction {kind (book, buy, sign_up, contact, enquire, call, visit, subscribe, download, other), label, target (a page path or https URL)}, successMeasures[]}.
motion {level (none, calm, lively, expressive; default calm), signature (the one memorable moment, in words), principles[] (up to 8 short rules), reducedMotion ("respect", always)}.
options? {motionFeel? (soft, crisp, springy, cinematic; default soft), copyMode? (what Build writes: placeholder, draft, keep; default draft; wireframes always use placeholder copy), voice? {use[]?, avoid[]? (up to 20 words or phrases each), readingLevel? (simple, standard, expert; default standard)}, internalLinks? (default true), externalLinks? (none, cite, recommend; default cite), visuals? (what fills image slots: placeholder, svg, mixed; default mixed)}: the owner's build options. Every field may be left out (its default applies); keep the ones the owner set.
sitemap[] {path, title, purpose, seo {title, description, keyword? (the main search phrase; leave it out on thank-you and legal pages), noindex? (true keeps the page out of search and the XML sitemap: thank-you and legal pages)}, children[]? (may be left out)}: "/" first. Site size counts content pages only; legal, thank-you and not-found pages come on top. A page that is on the site (wireframed or built) keeps its path and stays in the sitemap here: move or rename it with move_page (it carries its plan entry), and remove it from the site before the plan.
pages {"<path>": {sections[] {id (lowercase-dashes, unique on the page), type (from the section library, by group: opening: hero, page-header, announcement; story: about, story, mission, timeline; offer: features, benefits, services, menu, products, pricing, comparison; proof: testimonials, logos, stats, case-studies, reviews; people: team, careers; media: gallery, video, portfolio-list, portfolio-item; help: faq, process, contact, map, schedule, booking, form; content: blog-list, blog-post, events-list, event-item, content; close: cta, newsletter, footer-cta; any other short name is a custom type with no layouts), variant? (a layout of that type, listed by get_site_plan), motion? (reveal, stagger, parallax, marquee, pinned, counter, hover-lift, image-zoom, video-loop, page-transition, svg-draw, svg-morph, icon-motion, text-reveal, list-motion, beam, tilt-spotlight, scroll-story, ambient, none), visuals? (this section's image slots over options.visuals: placeholder, svg, mixed), list? {collection, filter?, limit?} (the section shows a collection's items), purpose, contentNotes} (each section's id is the data-section id of its element on the site), status (planned, wireframed, built; read from the site, keep what get_site_plan shows), inNav? (a hint used only when the menu is generated or inherited: absent means top-level pages in; legal, thank-you, nested and dynamic pages out; globals.nav.items decides the menu), navLabel? (a short menu label), prompt? (the owner's note for this page, keep it), template? (the page template it started from; template kinds: home, about, services, menu, pricing, contact, booking, events, blog-index, blog-post, portfolio-list, portfolio-item, faq, careers, legal, thank-you), collection? (a collections[] id: this is that collection's item page, path /<urlFolder>/:slug), localized? {"<locale>": {title, seo {title, description, keyword?}}}}}: localized holds other languages' title and SEO; each locale must be in audience.locales. pages merges by path: send only the pages you change (each entry you send replaces that page's whole entry), null removes one, and the entries of pages you take out of the sitemap go with them.
globals {nav {items[] {path, label? (left out: the page's navLabel, else its title), children[]? (page paths, one level; may be left out)}, links[]? {label, path and anchor (a section of a page: path "/" and anchor "features" is /#features; anchor alone is a section of the page being shown) or url (another site), at (its place: after that many items)} (menu links that aren't pages of their own; sync reads them from the site), cta? {label, path or url} (the one menu button; anchor? with path for a section of that page), layout (simple, centered, split, minimal), mobile (drawer, full-screen, inline), sticky, announcement? {text, path or url}}, footer {columns[] {title, links[] {label, path (with anchor? for a section of it) or url}}, contact, social, newsletter, legal[] (page paths as strings, such as "/privacy"; request texts show them resolved as {path, label}, but you write paths), layout (columns, simple, big-cta)}}: the shared nav and footer. nav.items is the menu, exactly as written: never "/" (the logo links home) and never the cta's page again as an item. Links point at sitemap pages (not dynamic ones) or https addresses; up to 12 menu items. Removing a page drops its links and renaming one keeps its place. Sending globals makes nav.items the menu as you wrote it; leaving globals out keeps them and lets new top-level pages join. Their status is read from the site (globalsStatus is optional), never set here.
library {sections[] {id, name, type, variant?, purpose, contentNotes, motion?, visuals?}, pages[] {id, name, purpose, sections[]}}: sections and pages the owner saved to reuse. Keep it unless asked.
collections[]? {id (lowercase-dashes, the content/<id> folder), name, purpose, starter? (blog, projects, team, products, events, jobs, testimonials, faq), fields[] {id (camelCase), type (CMS field types: plainText, richText, image, multiImage, videoLink, link, email, phone, number, date, dateTime, switch, color, option, file, reference, multiReference), label?, collection? (reference targets)}, urlFolder? (item pages on /<urlFolder>/:slug)}: CMS collections the site needs (blog, projects, team, menu, events...), up to 20. Each gets a collection page: a sitemap page on /<urlFolder>/:slug whose pages entry has collection: "<id>". A section that lists items has list {collection, filter? (in words, like "featured, newest first"), limit?}. Sync copies whether a collection exists, its fields and URL folder from the site (onSite marks it); purpose stays yours.
Icon sets (brand.iconSet takes a ui set; lucide, tabler, heroicons, phosphor, iconoir, mingcute, material-symbols, radix, bootstrap, line-md, simple-icons in all): get_site_plan lists each with its packages and when to use it.

branch.description: Default: the branch the workspace has open. Pass the request's branch when a request names one.

etag.description: The etag from your last get_site_plan; null when it said there is no plan file yet. Required with plan. Optional with pageStatus or globalsStatus alone (checked when you give it). A mismatch answers plan_conflict: read again and reapply your change.

globalsStatus.description: Instead of plan and pageStatus: the shared nav and footer's status, "wireframed" or "built" ("planned" resets it). Optional: Xodia reads it from the site when a globals request finishes.

path.description: The page's path in the sitemap, like /about

status.description: "planned", "wireframed" (grey boxes on the site) or "built" (designed and written)

path.description: The page's path in the sitemap, like /about

status.description: "planned", "wireframed" (grey boxes on the site) or "built" (designed and written)

pageStatus.description: Instead of plan: one page's status { path, status }, or a list of them. Optional: Xodia reads page statuses from the site (sync_site_plan, and after each request), so you don't need to set them.

plan.description: The plan (file version 2), or only the top-level fields you change: brief, inspiration, brand, audience, goals, motion, options, sitemap, pages, globals, library, collections. Fields you leave out keep their current values. version, updatedAt and updatedBy are set for you. Field shapes and allowed values are in the tool description.
